issues.legal_issue: A rent controller has discretion, rather than a duty, to strike out a tenant’s defence after the tenant fails to comply with an order to pay or deposit rent, and may allow delayed payment.
material_facts: The tenant had not paid rent and did not pay the arrears within the time directed by the Rent Controller.

The tenant later paid part of the arrears, but a balance remained outstanding; the Rent Controller found that the delay in depositing that balance was not wilful, deliberate, or contumacious and noted that there had been some compromise between the parties.
The matter was treated as a first default, and the Rent Controller condoned the delay and allowed the tenant the statutory protection against eviction.
The Tribunal and the High Court upheld that decision.
issues.conclusion: The Rent Controller was not required automatically to strike out the tenant’s defence for non-compliance with the payment order. The power to strike out the defence is discretionary, and the Controller may, after considering the circumstances, extend time or condone delay. The appeal was dismissed, leaving the tenant’s protection against eviction intact.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 14(1)(a), 14(2), 15(1), and 15(7) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, failure to comply with a rent-payment order does not itself require the defence to be struck out or eviction to follow. Section 15(7) says the Controller “may” strike out the defence, conferring discretion that must be exercised on the circumstances of the case and not mechanically. The Court applied Shyamcharan Sharma v. Dharamdas, which held under materially similar provisions that discretion not to strike out a defence implies discretion to condone default or extend time; Ram Murti v. Bhola Nath, which applied that principle to the Delhi Act; and Santosh Mehta v. Om Praksh, which treated the power as discretionary and the provision as directory and penal. Hem Chand v. Delhi Cloth & General Mills Co. Ltd. did not establish that non-compliance requires automatic eviction or mandatory striking out of the defence.

predicates.rent_arrears_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction on the ground that the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_follow_rent_payment_ord: The tenant did not pay or deposit rent as directed by the adjudicator.

issues.definition: When a tenant fails to follow a rent-payment order in an eviction proceeding based on rent arrears, the adjudicator may assess the circumstances and allow delayed payment without striking out the tenant’s defence.
